comment: The validate chain's cost, as data. FACTORY-SIDE ONLY — this file lives in scripts/ and
NO consumer gate reads it. That placement is the whole design: perf-baseline.json's own
header justifies its ratchet by saying 'Bytes are hardware-independent, so this check is
deterministic everywhere, agent time included'. Milliseconds are not. Shipping a
wall-clock ceiling into template/base/tools/ would put a machine-dependent verdict in a
consumer's turn, on hardware the harness has never seen.
These are the harness's own GitHub-hosted runner's numbers and they are NOT portable.
It replaces two inline shell literals in .github/workflows/selftest.yml ('-gt 120' with a
'-gt 90' warning). Those were not data, not versioned, not per-step, and not visible to
scripts/check-claims.mjs — so a chain that got slower produced an unattributed wall-clock
ceilingMs is a CHOSEN policy value and may ship. measuredMs is a MEASUREMENT and may not
be invented: it stays null until a real selftest run records one in a reviewed commit.
Until then check-claims.mjs refuses any wall-clock figure in README.md, which is why that
file still carries none. Measure, commit the measurement, then publish — in that order.

defaults.comment: A step with no row below is judged against its class ceiling. Class is decided by whether the step shells out to a toolchain (pnpm exec / tsc / next) or is pure node over the tree.
